Of course I can share! So, I use a command-line tool called wget, it's free software (as in price and freedom) developed by The GNU project. The gist of it is you can use this tool as follows from the terminal (Mac OS or Linux) and I believe you may also download it in Windows.

The command I use for creating perfect offline archives is: wget -mkEp https://www.website.com

You can replace the url with any url, just be sure to be specific (for example, voat.co doesn't use "www", so you would have to make sure not to include that). Also, sidenote, when running this command the files will be saved in your current directory, usually this is your Home folder by default (if you're running Mac OS or Linux) I'm not sure where this is by default for Windows. If you wish to change the location in Linux or Mac OS you can use the commands: cd (change directory) and mkdir (make directory) to create folders to keep everything organized if you want. Keeping it all in the default directory and then moving it afterwards is always an option as well, completely up to you!

The m, k, E and p parts are arguments that tell the tool to do different things. -m sets it in mirror mode, which enables a lot of settings which are useful when making a mirror of content. Things such as recursive downloading (where it automatically follows ALL links on that domain (website) and downloads everything from it, then keeps going until it no longer has anything left to download and you're ensured that you've downloaded everything. The -k argument tells the tool to convert all of the links to make them suitable for offline viewing, so that when you open your local copy and click on any of the links on the webpage, it doesn't try to take you to the online version of it. The -E argument makes sure that the correct filetypes are appended to the end of each file, otherwise they'd be stored as default "files" instead of something like file.html (which would allow you to open in your browser and view, as a normal site). And lastly, the -p argument tells the tool to download all of the requisite files for the webpage to work. Things such as images, the CSS formatting (what makes it look pretty) and sounds.
